The core idea revolves around leveraging the manifold hypothesis, which posits that real data resides on a lower-dimensional manifold within the high-dimensional data space. The authors propose that by operating within this manifold, generated samples can be guided towards specific conditions while maintaining high fidelity to the underlying data distribution. The MPGD framework is designed to be computationally efficient, requiring minimal additional inference cost for a broad range of tasks. The method operates by refining the guidance gradient within the tangent space of the manifold, effectively steering the generation process towards the desired condition without the need for task-specific training.
